title: Ocado said to be in early talks with Coles over robots in stores, shares jump
source_used: Australian Financial Review (AFR); first two paragraphs read, paywall after the lead
key_facts: Coles is exploring robots in its supermarkets to pick and pack grocery orders.
The aim is to cut costs and speed up delivery in the online battle with Woolworths.
Coles, led by chief executive Leah Weckert, is in early discussions with Ocado about trialling the technology in a Melbourne supermarket.
The report rests on sources familiar with the plans who asked not to be named.
No commercial agreement has been reached.
Ocado is a British delivery logistics group.
quote_evidence: Coles is exploring using robots in its supermarkets to pick and pack grocery orders, as it seeks to cut costs and accelerate delivery times in its online battle with Woolworths.
No commercial agreement has been reached.
why_it_matters_hint: Robots in stores would change how online orders are packed, which matters to shoppers and store staff.
